# Statement ledger

This ledger maps labels of the manuscript on the second moment of the
Stratonovich hyperbolic Anderson model with Gaussian noise fractional in time
to the Lean declarations in this package. Labels and TeX line numbers refer to
the manuscript revision a284420, and labels are written exactly as in its
LaTeX source (for example `P:clock-copy-obstruction`). The ledger was written
and reviewed at the earlier revisions cf979d6, 669ccc9, ba01d98, 3920258 and
975feb3. Revision a284420 makes two mathematical edits that the ledger
follows. (1) In `notes/integrated_spatial_occupation.tex` it adds Lemma
`L:spatial-fourier-bound` (lines 101-164, display `E:spatial-fourier-bound`),
the deterministic bound `A_sp(g) <= 2^(1+alpha) R_alpha b^(alpha/2)` that
`SpatialFourierBound` already proved, and the proof of
`P:spatial-smooth-ratio` (same label and statement) now derives `R_0 < inf`
from it, independently of the finiteness of `S_1^pos`, which it keeps only
for the score inequality. (2) In the main file, `L:damped-homogeneous-norms`
replaces its smoothing and truncation sentence by the multiplier comparison
`E:damped-multiplier-comparison` (a measurable multiplier `m` in `[0,1]`,
nested measurable Laplace domains, positivity after time integration,
scaling asserted only for the original covariance) and its proof by the
corresponding argument. The other changes since 975feb3 are prose and front
matter (title, abstract, preface, a theory-outlook chapter, the reader
edition, Appendices F and G, the list of notation moved to the back).
Every cited label exists exactly once at a284420. Three of them are new at
a284420 and do not exist at 975feb3: `L:spatial-fourier-bound`,
`E:spatial-fourier-bound` and `E:damped-multiplier-comparison`. Every other
cited label exists exactly once, in the same file, at both revisions, and
every such cited lemma, proposition, theorem, equation and section has the
same statement and proof up to whitespace and braces, except
`P:spatial-smooth-ratio` (proof only), `L:damped-homogeneous-norms`
(statement and proof) and the section `S:spatial-occupation-foundation`
(the new lemma). TeX line numbers were moved to a284420 by a line map; each
moved range has the same text at both revisions, and the ranges inside the
two edited passages were mapped to the corresponding new passages by hand
(script checks recorded in `provenance/manuscript-anchor.json`).

# Formalization scope

## The paper's argument and where Lean enters

The paper bounds and identifies the growth of `log E[u(t,x)²]` for the
Stratonovich hyperbolic Anderson model. The argument has three layers.

1. **Stochastic and analytic layer.** The chaos expansion, the two-chain
   pairing integrals, Wick pairings (beyond finite families of Gaussian
   values), Gaussian integration (beyond finitely many standard Gaussians),
   imported bounds,
   Laplace transforms and the variational asymptotics. **Not in Lean**,
   except a few slices: the Laplace transforms of the wave kernel and of
   the two-time kernel and the subordination formula (`ClockCopy` and its
   foundation modules), the Gaussian transform of the spectral measure
   (`MaskedSpectralGrowth`), the uniform scalar frequency row
   (`FrequencyRow`), the temporal completion `H_a` (`TimeCompletion`), the
   auxiliary mask norm (`MaskedAuxiliaryNorm`), the Gaussian heat envelope
   of the covariance (`VariationalMean`), a finite Hilbert-valued Bessel
   inequality (`PhaseBessel`), the wave Green measures `G_s` for
   `d = 1, 2, 3` (`WaveGreen`), the spectral identity and positive
   definiteness of `Gamma = delta_0(dx_1) dx_2` (`QuotientObstruction`), a
   finite Gaussian comparison under the positive semidefinite order
   (`GaussianComparison`), the two wave variance directions in spectral
   form (`WaveTwoVariances`), the variational floor and the Rayleigh-form
   rate (`VariationalFloor`, `VariationalRate`), the deterministic Fourier
   bound `L:spatial-fourier-bound` for the smooth spatial ratio and the
   static controls
   (`SpatialFourierBound`, `SpatialSmoothRatio`, `SpatialStaticControls`,
   `SpatialOccupationCompleted`), series types and the continuity of the
   growth types in the temporal exponent (`SeriesType`, `TypeContinuity`),
   the white-noise bound formulas and clock transforms
   (`WhiteRelativeWidth`, `WhiteClockLaplace`), the coefficient bound of
   the interval inventory product (`InventoryProduct`), an abstract `L^2`
   limit of a regularized series under a uniform scaled moment bound
   (`UniformSeriesTail`), the density of test functions in the
   weak-gradient `H^1` (`H1Density`), the physical four-linear extension
   and the spatial energy (`SpatialFourLinear`), the full physical
   occupation class (`OccupationPhysicalClass`; both completed in
   `SpatialOccupationL7Completed`), the scalar and Hilbert-space steps
   of the static interaction and interval coefficient bounds
   (`IntervalScalar`, `IntervalScalarCompleted`), the spectral-mass
   identity `R_Gamma(1) = R_alpha` (`SpectralMassIdentity`), Gaussian
   smoothing as a Fourier multiplier (`DampedMultiplier`), the positivity of
   the space-time occupation form, the deterministic occupation ceiling and
   the spatial bracket (`SpaceTimePositivity`, `OccupationCeilingFinite`,
   `SpatialBracket`, completed in `L8Completed`), the masked rates
   (`RemoveMask`), the finite Wick formula and the terminal-chain Wick
   formula with the chain measures given by their masses (`FiniteWick`,
   `TerminalWick`), an abstract compact Young baseline (`SymplecticFree`)
   and the Cauchy steps of the static phase orders (`StaticPhaseCauchy`),
   the Fourier transforms of the wave Green measures in `d = 1, 2, 3` and
   Archimedes' law for the sphere measure (`WaveGreenFourier`), the low-alpha
   convolution bound and the static contraction bounds
   (`LowAlphaConvolution`, `PhaseContractions`, completed in `L9Completed`),
   the exact occupation constant and ceiling (`RawOccupationEnergy`,
   `OccupationCeilingExact`), the normalized Hermite polynomials and the
   finite Gaussian Fock layer with values in a Hilbert factor
   (`GaussianHermite`, `HermiteFock`) and their consumers `L:fock-form`,
   `L:interval-contractions` and `E:occupied-multiplication` (`FockForm`),
   and the scalar and numerical-range steps of the complex phase bounds
   (`ComplexPhaseScalar`).
2. **Reductions to explicit inequalities.** At many points the analytic
   argument reduces to a finite statement: an exponent range, an exact
   rational or square-root inequality, a polynomial that must stay positive
   on a region, a determinant or matrix inverse, a count of coefficients in
   a finite word, or an integral comparison once integrability is known.
   **These are what Lean checks.**
3. **Assembly** of the main theorems from the layers above. **Not in Lean.**

So each module checks one reduction in layer 2. Its hypotheses state the
facts that layer 1 supplies (for example positivity of a parameter,
integrability of a function, or an inequality proved analytically in the
paper). Its conclusion is the fact that the paper then uses.

Heading categories (the same three are used in the statement ledger).
(A) "whole result": every conclusion of the labelled result is a Lean
conclusion under the manuscript's hypotheses, possibly with named supplied
inputs that are disclosed (coverage class same-assumptions or
inputs-supplied, conclusion full); no other module carries it. (B) "narrower
result: ...": a labelled result some of whose conclusions are not Lean
conclusions, or are proved for a modelled object (such as the class `O` by
joint representatives, or the rate in Rayleigh form and the cost in integral
form) whose identification with the manuscript's object is not formalized;
the heading names what is missing. (C) "foundation: ..." or "proof steps of
...": facts used by labelled results, not a labelled result themselves; the
`StratonovichHAMAudit` step modules are all of this kind.

Modules are counted by their ledger heading; a module that also proves
pieces of other results is counted once. Completion modules
(`ClockCopyHomog`, `MaskedContinuousWaveCompleted`, `L9Completed`,
`SpatialOccupationCompleted`, `SpatialOccupationL7Completed`,
`IntervalScalarCompleted`, `L8Completed`) discharge named inputs of other
modules; discharging an input does not make a narrower result whole, so
`L8Completed` (narrower results, except the whole result
`L:uniform-series-tail` with inputs supplied) and the spatial and occupation
modules remain "narrower result". `ClockCopyHomog`,
`MaskedContinuousWaveCompleted` and `TimeSchur`, which have no section of
their own, count as whole-result modules; `DampedNorms`, `SpectralHomog`,
`TimeFractional`, `WaveKernel`, `GaussianIBP`, `GaussianTest` and
`WeakSobolev` as foundations.

These counts describe the package. They are not a percentage of the paper.
The 31 whole results and 17 narrower results are deterministic lemmas,
propositions and corollaries used inside the analytic argument, and the
occupation ceiling `T:intrinsic-occupation-ceiling` (a narrower result: both
forms with the exact constant, for `S_c^pos`; `C_2 <= U_2` not formalized);
the other three main theorems are not formalized.

## Reading a statement

For each declaration, check three things against the paper:

1. the hypotheses match what the paper has available at that point;
2. the conclusion is what the paper uses next;
3. parameter ranges, strict versus non-strict inequalities and quantifier
   order agree.

The [statement ledger](docs/statement-ledger.md) records this for every row.
`Audit/<module>/` prints the full elaborated types, so the statements can be
read without opening an editor.

## Not yet included

Three development modules use a Gaussian-chaos library that is not yet
public: normalized Gaussian coordinates, vector Gaussian projection and
colored vector words. They are checked in the private development record
and will be added here when that library is released.

## Possible next steps

- the finite pair-partition counts behind the two-chain integrals;
- a reusable Laplace-to-time growth lemma, with its analytic inputs as
  hypotheses;
- the constant and exponent algebra of the main upper and lower bounds.

     8	1. **Stochastic and analytic layer.** The chaos expansion, the two-chain
     9	   pairing integrals, Wick pairings (beyond finite families of Gaussian
    10	   values), Gaussian integration (beyond finitely many standard Gaussians),
    11	   imported bounds,
    12	   Laplace transforms and the variational asymptotics. **Not in Lean**,
    13	   except a few slices: the Laplace transforms of the wave kernel and of
    14	   the two-time kernel and the subordination formula (`ClockCopy` and its
    15	   foundation modules), the Gaussian transform of the spectral measure
    16	   (`MaskedSpectralGrowth`), the uniform scalar frequency row
    17	   (`FrequencyRow`), the temporal completion `H_a` (`TimeCompletion`), the
    18	   auxiliary mask norm (`MaskedAuxiliaryNorm`), the Gaussian heat envelope
    19	   of the covariance (`VariationalMean`), a finite Hilbert-valued Bessel
    20	   inequality (`PhaseBessel`), the wave Green measures `G_s` for
    21	   `d = 1, 2, 3` (`WaveGreen`), the spectral identity and positive
    22	   definiteness of `Gamma = delta_0(dx_1) dx_2` (`QuotientObstruction`), a
    23	   finite Gaussian comparison under the positive semidefinite order
    24	   (`GaussianComparison`), the two wave variance directions in spectral
    25	   form (`WaveTwoVariances`), the variational floor and the Rayleigh-form
    26	   rate (`VariationalFloor`, `VariationalRate`), the deterministic Fourier
    27	   bound `L:spatial-fourier-bound` for the smooth spatial ratio and the
    28	   static controls
    29	   (`SpatialFourierBound`, `SpatialSmoothRatio`, `SpatialStaticControls`,
    30	   `SpatialOccupationCompleted`), series types and the continuity of the
    31	   growth types in the temporal exponent (`SeriesType`, `TypeContinuity`),
    32	   the white-noise bound formulas and clock transforms
    33	   (`WhiteRelativeWidth`, `WhiteClockLaplace`), the coefficient bound of
    34	   the interval inventory product (`InventoryProduct`), an abstract `L^2`
    35	   limit of a regularized series under a uniform scaled moment bound
    36	   (`UniformSeriesTail`), the density of test functions in the
    37	   weak-gradient `H^1` (`H1Density`), the physical four-linear extension
    38	   and the spatial energy (`SpatialFourLinear`), the full physical
    39	   occupation class (`OccupationPhysicalClass`; both completed in
    40	   `SpatialOccupationL7Completed`), the scalar and Hilbert-space steps
    41	   of the static interaction and interval coefficient bounds
    42	   (`IntervalScalar`, `IntervalScalarCompleted`), the spectral-mass
    43	   identity `R_Gamma(1) = R_alpha` (`SpectralMassIdentity`), Gaussian
    44	   smoothing as a Fourier multiplier (`DampedMultiplier`), the positivity of
    45	   the space-time occupation form, the deterministic occupation ceiling and
    46	   the spatial bracket (`SpaceTimePositivity`, `OccupationCeilingFinite`,
    47	   `SpatialBracket`, completed in `L8Completed`), the masked rates
    48	   (`RemoveMask`), the finite Wick formula and the terminal-chain Wick
    49	   formula with the chain measures given by their masses (`FiniteWick`,
    50	   `TerminalWick`), an abstract compact Young baseline (`SymplecticFree`)
    51	   and the Cauchy steps of the static phase orders (`StaticPhaseCauchy`),
    52	   the Fourier transforms of the wave Green measures in `d = 1, 2, 3` and
    53	   Archimedes' law for the sphere measure (`WaveGreenFourier`), the low-alpha
    54	   convolution bound and the static contraction bounds
    55	   (`LowAlphaConvolution`, `PhaseContractions`, completed in `L9Completed`),
    56	   the exact occupation constant and ceiling (`RawOccupationEnergy`,
    57	   `OccupationCeilingExact`), the normalized Hermite polynomials and the
    58	   finite Gaussian Fock layer with values in a Hilbert factor
    59	   (`GaussianHermite`, `HermiteFock`) and their consumers `L:fock-form`,
    60	   `L:interval-contractions` and `E:occupied-multiplication` (`FockForm`),
    61	   and the scalar and numerical-range steps of the complex phase bounds
    62	   (`ComplexPhaseScalar`).
    63	2. **Reductions to explicit inequalities.** At many points the analytic
    64	   argument reduces to a finite statement: an exponent range, an exact
    65	   rational or square-root inequality, a polynomial that must stay positive
    66	   on a region, a determinant or matrix inverse, a count of coefficients in
    67	   a finite word, or an integral comparison once integrability is known.
    68	   **These are what Lean checks.**
    69	3. **Assembly** of the main theorems from the layers above. **Not in Lean.**
    70	
    71	So each module checks one reduction in layer 2. Its hypotheses state the
    72	facts that layer 1 supplies (for example positivity of a parameter,
    73	integrability of a function, or an inequality proved analytically in the
    74	paper). Its conclusion is the fact that the paper then uses.

   124	## Reading a statement
   125	
   126	For each declaration, check three things against the paper:
   127	
   128	1. the hypotheses match what the paper has available at that point;
   129	2. the conclusion is what the paper uses next;
   130	3. parameter ranges, strict versus non-strict inequalities and quantifier
   131	   order agree.
   132	
   133	The [statement ledger](docs/statement-ledger.md) records this for every row.
   134	`Audit/<module>/` prints the full elaborated types, so the statements can be
   135	read without opening an editor.

     3	  210| We study the hyperbolic Anderson model
     4	  211| \cite{chen:author2026:time-dependency}*{(1.1)}
     5	  212| \begin{equation}\label{E:HAM}
     6	  213|   \frac{\partial^2 u}{\partial t^2}(t,x)=\Delta u(t,x)+\W(t,x)u(t,x),
     7	  214|   \qquad u(0,x)=1,\quad \frac{\partial u}{\partial t}(0,x)=0,
     8	  215| \end{equation}
     9	  216| for $(t,x) \in \R_+\times\R^d$, $d \in \{1,2,3\}$, interpreted in the
    10	  217| Stratonovich sense (limit of classical wave equations driven by smoothed noises
    11	  218| $\W_{\epsilon,\delta}$). The noise is centered Gaussian with
    12	  219| \begin{equation}\label{E:cov}
    13	  220|   \operatorname{Cov}\big(\W(s,x),\W(t,y)\big)=|s-t|^{-\alpha_0}\gamma(x-y),
    14	  221|   \qquad 0<\alpha_0<1,
    15	  222| \end{equation}
    16	  223| where $\gamma \ge 0$ is nonnegative definite with spectral measure $\mu$.
    17	  224| 
    18	  225| \begin{hypothesis}[Homogeneous covariance]\label{H:homog}
    19	  226|   Let $d \in \{1,2,3\}$ and $0 < \alpha_0 < 1$. The spatial covariance is a
    20	  227|   nonnegative, even, positive-definite tempered Radon measure $\Gamma$ on
    21	  228|   $\R^d$, with positive even tempered Radon spectral measure $\mu$ in the
    22	  229|   convention
    23	  230|   \[
    24	  231|     \Gamma=\int e^{i\xi\cdot x}\mu(\ud\xi)
    25	  232|     \quad\text{in the sense of tempered distributions}.
    26	  233|   \]
    27	  234|   The symbol $\gamma$ in~\eqref{E:cov} denotes this covariance as a function
    28	  235|   when one exists, and as a distribution otherwise. For every Borel set $A$ and
    29	  236|   $c > 0$, $\Gamma(cA) = c^{d-\alpha}\Gamma(A)$, and
    30	  237|   \begin{equation}\label{E:threshold}
    31	  238|     \alpha_0+\alpha<2,
    32	  239|   \end{equation}
    33	  240|   with $0 < \alpha < d$, or $\alpha = d = 1$. In particular, the last case
    34	  241|   includes spatial white noise $\Gamma = \delta_0$.
    35	  242| \end{hypothesis}
    36	  243| 
    37	  244| \paragraph{Zero covariance.}

    82	  803| \begin{lemma}[Homogeneous damped norms and temporal tails]
    83	  804|   \label{L:damped-homogeneous-norms}
    84	  805|   Under Hypothesis~\ref{H:homog}, the integrals
    85	  806|   in~\eqref{E:damped-norm-definitions} are finite for every $\theta > 0$, with
    86	  807|   $N_2(\theta)^2 \ge 0$, and
    87	  808|   \[
    88	  809|     N_0(\theta)=\theta^{-2},\qquad
    89	  810|     N_1(\theta)=\theta^{\alpha+\alpha_0-2}N_1(1),\qquad
    90	  811|     N_2(\theta)^2=\theta^{-\beta}N_2(1)^2,
    91	  812|     \quad\beta=4-\alpha-\alpha_0.
    92	  813|   \]
    93	  814|   Let
    94	  815|   \[
    95	  816|     K_M(r)=\frac1{\Gamma_{\mathrm{E}}(\alpha_0)}
    96	  817|     \int_M^\infty e^{-\lambda|r|}\lambda^{\alpha_0-1}\ud\lambda.
    97	  818|   \]
    98	  819|   Denote by $N_1^{(M)}(1)$ the first norm with $\lambda > M$, and by
    99	  820|   $N_2^{(M)}(1)$ the second norm with $K_M(s-t)$ in place of
   100	  821|   $|s-t|^{-\alpha_0}$. Then
   101	  822|   \begin{equation}\label{E:damped-tail-norms}
   102	  823|     N_1^{(M)}(1)\longrightarrow0,\qquad
   103	  824|     N_2^{(M)}(1)\longrightarrow0\quad(M\to\infty).
   104	  825|   \end{equation}
   105	  826|   More precisely, let $m:\R^d\to[0,1]$ be measurable and let
   106	  827|   $S\subset S'\subset(0,\infty)$ be measurable. Define $N_{1,m,S}(\theta)$
   107	  828|   by replacing $\mu$ with $m\mu$ and restricting the $\lambda$ integral in
   108	  829|   $N_1$ to $S$. Define $N_{2,m,S}(\theta)^2$ by replacing $\mu$ with $m\mu$
   109	  830|   and the temporal kernel in $N_2^2$ with
   110	  831|   \[
   111	  832|     K_S(r)=\frac1{\Gamma_{\mathrm{E}}(\alpha_0)}
   112	  833|     \int_S e^{-\lambda|r|}\lambda^{\alpha_0-1}\ud\lambda.
   113	  834|   \]
   114	  835|   Then, for every $\theta>0$,
   115	  836|   \begin{equation}\label{E:damped-multiplier-comparison}
   116	  837|     \begin{split}
   117	  838|       0\le N_{1,m,S}(\theta)&\le N_{1,1,S'}(\theta),\\
   118	  839|       0\le N_{2,m,S}(\theta)^2&\le N_{2,1,S'}(\theta)^2.
   119	  840|     \end{split}
   120	  841|   \end{equation}
   121	  842|   These are comparisons of spectral expressions, including full and tail
   122	  843|   domains. An arbitrary $m$ need not preserve Hypothesis~\ref{H:homog}; the
   123	  844|   scaling identities above are asserted for the original covariance only.
   124	  845|   Spatial Gaussian smoothing and Gaussian smoothing of the Green kernel
   125	  846|   give multipliers in this class. The separate mass identity for $N_0$ is
   126	  847|   unchanged by Gaussian smoothing of the Green kernel.
   127	  848| \end{lemma}

   130	 1773| \begin{proposition}[Mild construction from the fixed-order limits]
   131	 1774|   \label{P:mild-construction}
   132	 1775|   Under Hypothesis~\ref{H:homog}, the series $u(t,x) = \sum_{n\ge0}X_n(t,x)$ is
   133	 1776|   a mild solution in~\cite{chen:author2026:time-dependency}*{Definition~2.1 and
   134	 1777|   (2.12), pp.~9--10}. More precisely, for each $t > 0$ and $x \in \R^d$,
   135	 1778|   \begin{equation}\label{E:mild-construction}
   136	 1779|     \lim_{\epsilon,\delta\downarrow0}
   137	 1780|     \int_0^t\int_{\R^d}G(t-s,x-\ud y)
   138	 1781|     u(s,y)W_{\epsilon,\delta}(s,y)\ud s
   139	 1782|     =u(t,x)-1\quad\text{in }L^2(\Omega).
   140	 1783|   \end{equation}
   141	 1784|   The limit allows arbitrary relative rates of the two widths. In dimension
   142	 1785|   three the Green-width limit precedes the noise-width limit. No uniqueness
   143	 1786|   assertion is made.
   144	 1787| \end{proposition}

     5	amplitude. Set $a = \alpha_0$, $k = 3-\alpha > 1$, $q = 4-\alpha = k+1$ and $D =
     6	q-2a > 0$. The scalar $D$ is fixed. All profiles are real. The original positive

    10	Proposition~\ref{P:variational-positive-scores}.
    11	
    12	\begin{lemma}[The physical two-point integral]\label{L:spatial-physical-pair}
    13	  The positive measure $\nu(\ud x,\ud y) = \ud x\,\Gamma(\ud y)$ is
    14	  sigma-finite. For nonnegative functions define
    15	  \begin{equation}\label{E:spatial-physical-pair}
    16	    B_\Gamma(f,h)=\int f(x)h(x-y)\nu(\ud x,\ud y)
    17	  \end{equation}
    18	  initially as an extended nonnegative integral, using finite Borel
    19	  representatives of Lebesgue classes. Its value is representative independent.
    20	  Lebesgue-a.e. convergence transfers to $\nu$-a.e. convergence at both
    21	  positions $x$ and $x-y$.
    22	\end{lemma}
    23	
    24	\begin{proof}
    25	  Local finiteness of $\Gamma$ gives sigma-finiteness on exhausting balls, and
    26	  Lebesgue measure is sigma-finite. If $N$ is Borel and Lebesgue null, Tonelli
    27	  applied first in $x$ gives $\nu\{x\in N\} = 0$ and $\nu\{x-y\in N\} = 0$,
    28	  because every fixed translate of $N$ is null. An arbitrary Lebesgue null set
    29	  has a Borel null superset. Thus, arbitrary versions are measurable in the
    30	  $\nu$ completion with the same value, and the same observation applies to the
    31	  exceptional sets of a.e. convergence. Signed pairings will be used only after
    32	  absolute convergence. This proves Lemma~\ref{L:spatial-physical-pair}.
    33	\end{proof}
    34	
    35	Put $A_{\mathrm{sp}}(g) = B_\Gamma(g^2,g^2)$ and $b(g) = \|\nabla g\|_2^2$ on

    37	before the extension below. For smooth compact $z$, write $U_z = \Gamma*z$ in

    40	\begin{lemma}[Smooth temporal controls]\label{L:spatial-static-controls}
    41	  For every nonnegative nonzero $z \in C_c^\infty(\R^d)$, let
    42	  \[
    43	    \lambda_z(c)^2=
    44	    \sup_{\substack{g\in H^1(\R^d;\R)\\\|g\|_2=1}}
    45	    \left(c\int U_zg^2-b(g)\right),\qquad c>0.
    46	  \]

   350	\subsection{The kernel row and full occupation energy}
   351	
   352	Define, for $u \ne 0$,
   353	\begin{equation}\label{E:occupation-damped-kernel}
   354	  K_\star(u)=\frac1{\Gamma_E(a)}
   355	  \int_0^\infty
   356	  e^{-(\lambda+\lambda^2/(2D))|u|}
   357	  \lambda^{a-1}\ud\lambda,
   358	\end{equation}
   359	and set $K_\star(0) = 0$ for time integration.
   360	
   361	\begin{lemma}[Exact row maximum]\label{L:occupation-kernel-row}
   362	  The kernel is even, positive off zero, locally integrable, decreasing on
   363	  $(0,\infty)$, and $K_\star(u) \le |u|^{-a}$ off zero. Its exact row maximum on
   364	  $[0,1]$ is
   365	  \begin{equation}\label{E:occupation-kernel-row}
   366	    \max_{s\in[0,1]}\int_0^1K_\star(s-t)\ud t
   367	    =R_\star:=2\int_0^{1/2}K_\star(u)\ud u\in(0,\infty).
   368	  \end{equation}
   369	\end{lemma}
   370	
   371	\begin{proof}
   372	  Dropping the positive quadratic damping bounds the mixture by the Gamma
   373	  integral $|u|^{-a}$. Positivity and monotonicity follow directly from the
   374	  integrand, and $a < 1$ gives local integrability. Put $\Phi(t) =
   375	  \int_0^tK_\star(u)\ud u$. It is concave because its integrand is decreasing on
   376	  positive arguments. The row is $\Phi(s)+\Phi(1-s) \le 2\Phi(1/2)$, with
   377	  equality at $s = 1/2$. The diagonal value changes no time integral. This
   378	  proves Lemma~\ref{L:occupation-kernel-row}.
   379	\end{proof}
   380	
   381	Let $\mathcal{O}$ be the full class of strongly $H^1(\R^d;\R)$-measurable fields
   382	$s\mapsto g_s$ on $(0,1)$ with $\|g_s\|_2 = 1$ a.e. and $T(g) =
   383	\int_0^1b(g_s)\ud s < \infty$. No time smoothness, common compact support or
   384	optimizer condition is imposed.
   385	
   386	\begin{proposition}[The full physical occupation class]
   387	  \label{P:occupation-physical-class}
   388	  The pairings $(s,t)\mapsto B_\Gamma(g_s^2,g_t^2)$ are measurable,
   389	  representative independent and equal to their physical integrals. With
   390	  \[
   391	    J(g)=\int_0^1\int_0^1
   392	    K_\star(s-t)B_\Gamma(g_s^2,g_t^2)\ud s\ud t,
   393	  \]
   394	  every $g \in \mathcal{O}$ satisfies
   395	  \begin{equation}\label{E:occupation-physical-bound}
   396	    0\le J(g)\le R_\star R_{\mathrm{sp}}T(g)^{\alpha/2}<\infty.
   397	  \end{equation}
   398	  The energy over exactly this full class satisfies
   399	  \begin{equation}\label{E:occupation-own-energy}
   400	    0<\mathcal{E}_\star^{\mathcal{O}}
   401	    :=\sup_{g\in\mathcal{O}}\big(J(g)-T(g)/2\big)
   402	    \le R_\star^{2/(2-\alpha)}\mathcal{E}_{\mathrm{sp}}<\infty.
   403	  \end{equation}
   404	\end{proposition}

  3600	\begin{lemma}[The finite terminal-chain Wick formula]\label{L:terminal-wick}
  3601	  Let $\mathcal{W}(s,y)$ be a centered real Gaussian field on $[0,T]\times\R^d$,
  3602	  $d = 1,2,3$, with covariance $\mathcal{K}(s,y;r,z)$. Suppose that $V =
  3603	  \sup_{s,y}\E|\mathcal{W}(s,y)|^2 < \infty$, and that the field is jointly
  3604	  continuous in mean square on each open cell of a finite partition of $[0,T]$,
  3605	  times $\R^d$. Define $Y_0 = 1$ and
  3606	  \[
  3607	    Y_n(T,x)=\int\prod_{j=1}^n\mathcal{W}(s_j,y_j)
  3608	    \,\mathsf{g}_n^{T,x}(\ud\boldsymbol s,\ud\boldsymbol y).
  3609	  \]
  3610	  These Bochner integrals exist in $L^2(\Omega)$ and satisfy
  3611	  \begin{equation}\label{E:terminal-term-majorant}
  3612	    \|Y_n(T,x)\|_2
  3613	    \le\sqrt{(2n-1)!!}\,V^{n/2}\frac{T^{2n}}{(2n)!},
  3614	    \qquad n\ge1.
  3615	  \end{equation}
  3616	  For $m+n = 2k$, concatenate $\boldsymbol\tau =
  3617	  (s_1,\ldots,s_m,r_1,\ldots,r_n)$ and $\boldsymbol\eta =
  3618	  (y_1,\ldots,y_m,z_1,\ldots,z_n)$. Then
  3619	  \begin{equation}\label{E:terminal-wick-formula}
  3620	    \E[Y_m(T,x)Y_n(T,x)]
  3621	    =\sum_{D\in\Pi_k}\mathcal{T}_{m,n,D}^{\mathcal{K}}(T,x),
  3622	  \end{equation}
  3623	  where, with both chains terminating at $(T,x)$,
  3624	  \begin{equation}\label{E:terminal-pairing-integral}
  3625	    \begin{split}
  3626	      \mathcal{T}_{m,n,D}^{\mathcal{K}}
  3627	      ={}&\int_{[0,T]^m_<\times[0,T]^n_<}
  3628	      \ud\boldsymbol s\,\ud\boldsymbol r
  3629	      \int_{(\R^d)^m\times(\R^d)^n}\\
  3630	      &\quad\times\prod_{j=1}^m
  3631	      G_{s_{j+1}-s_j}(y_{j+1}-\ud y_j)
  3632	      \prod_{j=1}^n
  3633	      G_{r_{j+1}-r_j}(z_{j+1}-\ud z_j)\\
  3634	      &\quad\times\prod_{\{a,b\}\in D}
  3635	      \mathcal{K}(\tau_a,\eta_a;\tau_b,\eta_b).
  3636	    \end{split}
  3637	  \end{equation}

  3639	  Empty chains and the case $m = n = 0$ have the usual empty-product meaning. If

  3641	  entrywise comparison $0 \le \mathcal{K}_1 \le \mathcal{K}_2$ compares all
